name: matriliny

attributes.attribute: a Celtic method of descent through the mother line
used by rulers and heroes who bore matrilineal names
a possible remnant of the culture of the Picts

sources: Dexter, Miriam Robbins. “Queen Medb, Female Autonomy in Ancient Ireland, and Irish Matrilineal Traditions.” In Proceedings of the Ninth Annual Ucla Indo-European Conference, edited by Karlene Jones-Bley, Angela Della Volpe, Miriam Robbins Dexter, and Martin E. Huld, 95–122. Washington, D.C.: Institute for the Study of Man, 1998.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matriliny, or matrilineality, was the tracing of descent through the mother line. It is one of the most contentious areas of modern research into the Celts. Scholars ask whether Celtic women were freer than the women of other peoples of their time, or whether the view only projects a hope onto ancient cultures. Those who see greater rights note that many Celtic heroes carried their mother's names. The king of Ulster, Conchobar mac Nessa, took his name from his mother Nessa. The king of Connacht took his from his mother Mata. The hero Diarmait Ua Duibne took his from a maternal ancestor. In Wales, Mabon was called the son of the Mother, and king Math's throne went to his sister's son. Matriliny does not prove greater rights, but it suggests a different pattern of gender relations. Some propose it was a leftover from the earlier people called the Picts.
objective: Document matriliny, the tracing of Celtic descent through the mother line.
key_results: Record the meaning of matriliny as descent through the mother line.
Record the heroes who bore matrilineal names.
Record the views on women's rights they imply.
Record the possible origin among the Picts.
